title: Intradural extramedullary venous hemangioma mimicking meningioma: a case report and literature review.

title: Portable polysomnography-derived multi-domain EEG markers of anesthetic state transitions during propofol anesthesia for gastrointestinal endoscopy.
summary: Propofol anesthesia is widely used for gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy, but electroencephalographic (EEG) features of anesthetic state transitions in this brief and stimulus-rich setting remain incompletely characterized. title: Dynamics-informed machine learning for recovering extensive missing systems dynamics.
summary: Inevitable missing values in observational time series often hinder reliable data-driven modeling of complex systems across diverse domains. summary: Extensive longitudinal neuroimaging research has investigated brain structural and functional changes following electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) for depression. title: An insular-orbitofrontal pathway supporting awareness of respiratory effort.
summary: In a recent study using human intracranial EEG recordings during inspiratory loading, Assi and colleagues identified parallel pathways for respiratory compensation and awareness. The anterior insula signals a neuromechanical mismatch to the orbitofrontal cortex for conscious appraisal, while high-frequency insular-frontal coupling enables ventilatory adjustments. The findings are highly relevant for disorders of altered respiratory perception.

title: Mobile EEG Reveals Age-Dependent Cognitive-Motor Interference with Increasing Motor Task Complexity- a cross-sectional study.
summary: This study examined age-related differences in behavior and brain dynamics underlying cognitive-motor interference (CMI) during motor dual-tasks (DT) with increasing motor task complexity. summary: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is a network disorder extending beyond the structurally defined epileptogenic zone. summary: Generalized spike-wave discharges (GSWD) are occasionally observed in patients with self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS), but their clinical significance remains unclear. summary: Perception reflects the dynamic integration of prior expectations, uncertainty, and incoming sensory evidence, but the neural circuitry supporting these computations remains debated. summary: Infantile amnesia, the inability to recall memories from our earliest years, is the most common form of forgetting in mammals. title: CNN-based classifier for subject-independent MBTI Extraversion/Introversion preference classification from short-time EEG signals
summary: This study examines whether short, minimally preprocessed EEG segments contain sufficient information to distinguish between individuals classified as extraverted or introverted according to the Myers--Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI). summary: We investigate whether a 2D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on minimally preprocessed EEG signals can classify hypnotic susceptibility across distinct brain regions.
